newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S. envoy to Mexico to work for manufacturer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy to Mexico to work for manufacturer.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador to Mexico James Jones is to leave government service and head the international division of a major U.S. apparel manufacturing group, the company announced on Monday.

Jones, who has served as Washington's envoy to Mexico since 1993, has still not officially announced a leaving date from his current job, though he is expected to leave in late June, embassy officials said.

But the New York-based Warnaco Group said in a statement that Jones "has been appointed president of its international division effective July 1, 1997." Warnaco makes Fruit of the Loom bras, Calvin Klein men's underwear, Bodyslimmers and other intimate apparel.

"Jim has an extensive background, including 30 years experience in business, government and international affairs, and is well qualified to lead our efforts to globalize this corporation," Warnaco said.

The Mexico City embassy is one of Washington's largest and its head has a particularly difficult job because of Mexico's often prickly relations with its huge northern neighbour, upset by constant spats over drug trafficking and immigration.
A former CEO of the American Stock Exchange, Jones is a major figure in Mexico. Local reporters follow all his public appearances and avidly report his comments.

President Bill Clinton has tapped William Weld, the Republican governor of Massachusetts, to replace Jones but Weld has yet to be confirmed by the Senate. Some congressmen have criticised Weld's appointment, claiming that he once favoured the medicinal use of marijuana and is therefore unsuitable for posting to a major drug producing and trafficking nation like Mexico.
Hispanic legislators have also complained that Weld lacks knowledge of Mexico.
